t: You're at Cleveland Square, a private, gated garden square in Bayswater, north of Hyde Park. Around it are tall, tree-shaded rows of stuccoed houses with pillared porches. Several people have connections to the square. The solicitor and inventor John Bethell died here. He patented the Bethell process, which preserved timber with creosote under pressure and gave it a life of twenty-five years or more, which mattered for railway sleepers and telegraph poles. The politician Charles Manners Lushington was born here, and so was the artist Bessie Hamilton Johnston.
